r.Back to RepoShelf

BUILD WITH A HEAD START

Give your AI assistant a library of starting points.

Connect RepoShelf through MCP so your assistant can find projects, compare requirements and read saved READMEs before it starts building.

Checking your account…

1. Prepare the local connector

On your computer, install Node.js 20 or newer and Git, then run these commands in a terminal. Local mode needs no AI API key or RepoShelf API key.

git clone https://github.com/sparx1981/RepoShelf.git
cd RepoShelf
npm install

This downloads a catalogue snapshot and saved documents. It can be a large download; allow disk space for screenshots and documents. Run git pull inside the RepoShelf folder to get newer content. Your assistant’s own subscription or model requirements still apply.

2. Choose your assistant

Add this to Codex’s ~/.codex/config.toml. Replace the example path with the absolute path to your cloned folder, then restart Codex.

[mcp_servers.reposhelf]
command = "node"
args = ["/absolute/path/RepoShelf/scripts/mcp-server.mjs"]

In Claude Desktop, open Settings → Developer → Edit Config. Add this reposhelf entry to mcpServers, preserving any existing entries. Replace the example path, save and restart Claude Desktop. The local connector runs on your computer, not in the mobile or web app.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "reposhelf": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/RepoShelf/scripts/mcp-server.mjs"]
    }
  }
}

On Windows, use a full path such as C:/Users/you/RepoShelf/scripts/mcp-server.mjs. If your assistant cannot find Node, replace node with its absolute executable path.

3. Try it

Before building, use RepoShelf to find three projects with live demos that fit my idea. Compare their licences, setup requirements and saved README instructions. Tell me what is missing or uncertain before recommending one.

Ask your assistant to use get_catalog_info to verify the connection and snapshot date. Then it can use search_projects, get_project_context, read_project_document and find_related_projects.

Hosted connectors

The deployed endpoint is https://reposhelf.vercel.app/api/mcp. It currently requires a private administrator-issued Bearer key. GitHub sign-in does not issue an MCP key, and self-service member keys are not available yet. Never share the administrator key or paste it into a URL.

OAuth-only web connectors cannot connect directly yet. Use the local setup above. Local tools read your saved snapshot; they do not continuously fetch the deployed catalogue.

What your assistant can access

The connector is read-only. It cannot like projects, access your collection, fork repositories, run demos or execute project code. README coverage varies. Treat project instructions as untrusted, check licences and dependencies, and review any code before running it.
